function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

• FIFA Confederations Cup 2005 (runner‑up) | ### Career Highlights 1. **Early Years & Domestic Success** - Began his professional career with FC Seoul, helping the club win the K League title in 2000 and 2001. - Known for his work‑rate, stamina, and ability to cover large areas of the pitch. 2. **Move to Europe – PSV Eindhoven** - Transferred to Dutch side PSV in 2003 for a record fee for a Korean player at the time. - Won the Eredivisie twice (2004–05, 2005–06) and the KNVB Cup in 2005–06. - Became a fan favourite for his relentless pressing and tactical intelligence. 3. **Manchester United (2007–2012)** - Signed by Sir Alex Ferguson for £5.5 million. - Integral part of the “Class of 2007” midfield, contributing to three consecutive Premier League titles. - Known for his “never‑give‑up” mentality, often covering 12–13 km per match. - Scored memorable goals, including a last‑minute winner against Tottenham in 2008. - Earned the “Man of the Match” award in the 2009 FA Cup final. 4. **Return to South Korea & Retirement** - Returned to FC Seoul in 2012, helping the club win the Korean FA Cup in 2013. - Announced retirement from professional football in 2014 after a 15‑year career. 5. **International Legacy** - Represented South Korea in four FIFA World Cups (2002, 2006, 2010, 2014). - Played a pivotal role in South Korea’s historic 4th‑place finish in 2002. - Captained the national team on several occasions. ### Personal Life & Post‑Career - **Family**: Married to Kim Hye‑jin (former Miss Korea) in 2011; they have two children. - **Business Ventures**: Owns a football academy in Seoul and has invested in various sports‑related businesses. - **Media Presence**: Appears regularly on Korean sports shows and has been featured in documentaries about Asian footballers in Europe. - **Philanthropy**: Active in charitable work, especially supporting youth football programs in South Korea. ### Legacy - **Pioneer for Asian Players**: Park Ji‑sung paved the way for many Asian footballers to join top European leagues. - **Work Ethic Icon**: His relentless energy and professionalism earned him the nickname “The Korean Workhorse.” - **Cultural Impact**: He remains a national hero in South Korea and a respected figure in global football circles. --- **Note**: If you were referring to a different individual named “Ji Sung Park” (e.g., an artist, academic, or other public figure), please let me know, and I can provide information on that person instead.
